terms.latin: contrā dīcō, contrā dīcere, contrā dīxī, contrā dictum
terms.grammar: verb with a dative; written as two words before the post-Augustan period
evidence: Lewis & Short s.v. contrādīcō: “until the post-Aug. per. always written as two words”
terms.comment: Traupman: contrādīcere (+ dat.). To contradict oneself is pugnantia loquī (see contradict oneself).

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency (printed page numbers): p. 296.
